Literal patterns match only (), null and Nats.

case "E" never matches, and neither do case true, case (-1) or case 0.5: the grammar takes any literal in a pattern, but pattern_matches (vm_match.rs) has arms only for Unit, Null and Nat, so the rest fall through to no match, silently. Until fixed: test with == in an if.
An arm for every literal: Text, Bool, Char, Int (a negative literal is UnOpLiteral), and Float by value; a pattern of a kind that can never match its value an error, not a quiet miss.
Nat and Int mix in some places and not others.

- mixes them (a Nat minus a larger Nat is an Int, as it should be), but +, *, / and % do not, and Int + Nat is worse than an error: it falls to try_symbolic_binop and comes back as the unevaluated expression -2 + 1. < mixes them; <=, > and >= are not implemented. Int(4) == Nat(4) is false, and they are different map keys.

One rule for whole numbers: a result of 0 or more is always a Nat, below 0 always an Int (as - already does), for every operation; arithmetic and all six comparisons defined for every pair; so == and a map's keys agree by value. A symbolic result only when an operand is symbolic.

0.25 < 0.5 stops: <, <=, > and >= have no Float arm. Found porting the Trap room, whose random wiring compares draws with 0.5; matthewhammer/kids-choice-games#4 passes the draws as Nats in millionths instead, so the rule's globals no longer match Hazel's.
The four comparisons on Floats, and between a Float and a Nat or an Int (as + already mixes Float and Nat); then the game's draws go back to Floats.
"a" < "b" stops. A map keyed by text (a lever's id) wants it; Hazel has string_compare.
